summary: Role-aware SIEM stream with contextual field-level redaction and SOC2 control mapping
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (FinSight Analytics) requests a role-aware SIEM export that delivers both operator-safe and SOC analyst-safe event feeds simultaneously. The feed must support contextual field-level redaction rules that vary by consumer role, include geo-IP and K8s pod-label enrichment, guarantee per-event HMAC with rotating KEK, and provide ordering (+dedupe) guarantees for incident reconstruction.

Impact:
Customer cannot onboard Redwood audit data into their SOC until they get a signed sample stream and a controls mapping for SOC2. This blocks their internal security assessment and an audit kickoff scheduled next week.

Environment:
prod-us-east primary stream, customer uses dedicated ingestion consumer into an S3 bucket in their AWS account. They require server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (SSE-KMS) and presigned delivery manifests.

Steps to reproduce / requested deliverables:
1) Provide a 1-hour signed sample stream containing both operator-view and analyst-view events for tenant fin_sight (anonymized tenant id).
2) Sample must include: request/response tokens (redacted), user_id pseudonymized (consistent mapping), IP->geo enrichment fields, pod_name and instance_id, and redaction metadata describing which rule applied.
3) Provide per-event HMAC header and a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and a KEK rotation snapshot.
4) Deliver a SOC2 control mapping document that maps exported fields and our redaction approach to relevant SOC2 CC criteria (evidence for CC6, CC7, CC8).
5) Provide a brief runbook for the customer's SOC on how to verify HMACs and rehydrate pseudonyms during an investigation.

Logs / sample payloads:
Customer shared a daytime sample of their ingestion flow (attached in ticket). They reported missing geo fields on ~18% of events and intermittent HMAC mismatches for events where the connector retried.

Customer deadline: audit kickoff planned 2026-03-18.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (reporter): Customer emailed security@redwood asking for role-specific redaction examples and an evidence pack for SOC2. Attached: their SIEM mapping template and example object storage policy.

2026-03-10 09:45 - Samantha Patel (assigned): Acknowledged receipt. Requested 1-hour live capture and S3 write access (cross-account role or presigned URL). Opened internal INT-412 for engineering support on HMAC and redaction logic.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Luis Ramirez (SRE): Noted that geo-IP enrichment uses our external service which had a 503 spike at 03:00 UTC; will check correlation. Suggested enabling local fallback enrichment for missing geo fields.
2026-03-11 15:24 - Customer (FinSight SOC lead): Provided sample S3 bucket and IAM role; asked that redaction schema include a column explaining why a field was removed (policy id).

2026-03-12 10:40 - Samantha Patel: Delivered presigned S3 upload for 1-hour capture and confirmed encryption settings. Engineering will provide the signed manifest and the control mapping by EOD 2026-03-12 (tentative).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10: Reproduced missing geo fields locally against provided sample. Observed 18% null geo when the enrichment service returned 5xx; enrichment is non-blocking so events still emitted without geo. Hypothesis: intermittent enrichment backend outage explains customer missing geo fields.

2026-03-10: Observed HMAC mismatches in customer's sample where event timestamps differ by >1s between our connector and their consumer (retries collapsed). Hypothesis: connector retry behavior altered canonical ordering before HMAC signing. Need to ensure signing occurs after final canonicalization and before retry aggregation.

2026-03-11: Created engineering spike PR to move HMAC signing to post-dedup stage and attach a nonce per-emit (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1214). This should stop mismatches caused by in-flight retries.

2026-03-11: Implemented a mapping table for role-based redaction rules. Ruleset examples: ROLE=operator -> redact: user.email, request_prompts; ROLE=soc_analyst -> redact: request_prompts only. Each rule emits a redaction_reason field (e.g., 'pii-policy-1').
2026-03-12: Confirmed SSE-KMS headers and presigned manifest generation flow against customer's S3. Verified the manifest includes per-file SHA256 and KEK version id.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Delivered the 1-hour signed sample bundle to customer's presigned S3 URL. Bundle contains two folders: operator_view/ and soc_analyst_view/ with mirrored events; each event includes redaction_reason, hmac, nonce, and enrichment fields. Presigned URL: (redacted in ticket).

2026-03-12: Engineering deployed PR #1214 to staging, which moves HMAC signing to post-dedup and adds a per-emit nonce. Will schedule a production rollout behind a feature flag and coordinate with the customer for a short maintenance window.

Provided SOC2 mapping doc: attached as 'soc2_control_mapping_fin_sight_v1.pdf' in ticket. Mapped exported fields to SOC2 CC6/CC7/CC8 and included suggested evidence collection steps (console screenshots, manifest checksums, KMS rotation logs).

Workaround / next steps: For immediate audit needs, we provided a signed sample and a validation script that FinSight can run to verify HMACs and checksums. For ongoing production: recommend Dedicated plan with guaranteed delivery SLAs and an agreed weekly signed snapshot export. Engineering follow-up INT-412 tracks production rollout and KEK rotation automation.

Follow-up: Customer requested a short runbook and a 30-minute walkthrough with our Security PM. Meeting scheduled for 2026-03-14. Legal will coordinate on any formal evidence/legal attestation if auditor requests vendor letter.
